messages.subject: pre-built program not found
parts:
Hello,

I'm creating a package with 2 pre-built Stan programs. The first Stan program runs fine, but the second one is failing with the following error message:

Error in get(paste0("model_", model_cppname)) :
  object 'model_poisson' not found
>
> traceback()
6: get(paste0("model_", model_cppname))
5: object@mk_cppmodule(object)
4: .local(object, ...)
3: sampling(stanfit, data = stan_data, iter = iter, warmup = warmup,
       chains = chains, seed = seed, cores = cores, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))
2: sampling(stanfit, data = stan_data, iter = iter, warmup = warmup,
       chains = chains, seed = seed, cores = cores, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))
1: check_incidence(sim_list, iter = 200, warmup = 25, chains = 2,
       cores = 2, seed = 123, nsimul = 1)

I believe it's not finding the second Stan program. Any hint to find what could be wrong? Thanks!

Denis

On Monday, July 25, 2016 at 3:03:04 PM UTC-4, Denis Haine wrote:
I'm creating a package with 2 pre-built Stan programs. The first Stan program runs fine, but the second one is failing with the following error message:

Have you called rstan::rstan.package.skeleton("package_name") and followed the steps in the Read-And-Delete-Me file it creates? That is the only method for creating a package with pre-built Stan models that is known to be reliable.

Ben

Pretty sure I'm missing something trivial.

Denis

On Tuesday, July 26, 2016 at 8:51:52 AM UTC-4, Denis Haine wrote:
Yes I did. The package was working fine when with only one Stan program (and stll running ok with this particular one). R CMD check did not report any error. I added stan_fit4Modelname_mod for the 2 models in the RccModules in DESCRIPTION file; add the useDynLib to NAMESPACE. The 2 models appear in Modules.cpp and models.hpp. I'm calling both models the same way in each function (stanfit <- stanmodels$ModelName).
Pretty sure I'm missing something trivial.

Try putting this newer .onLoad() function into R/zzz.R

.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  modules <- paste0("stan_fit4", names(stanmodels), "_mod")
  for (m in modules) loadModule(m, what = TRUE)
}

The old way of calling loadModules() and putting entries into the DESCRIPTION file was deprecated by Rcpp anyway.

Ben

On Tuesday, July 26, 2016 at 12:06:00 PM UTC-4, Denis Haine wrote:
I replaced my old zzz.R by yours. Not sure if I have to remove also the RcppModules line in DESCRIPTION. Both models failed now, with the following message:

What version of R are you using? For rstanarm, we have to run R CMD check only using 1 core to do the MCMC and tests in order to avoid a similar error message. When it uses multiple cores / subprocesses, it seems to find a previously installed version of the package on disk that may or may not be up to date with the version of the package currently being checked.

Ben

Sorry for the inconvenience, it's only my second package and it's not easy to grasp the use of namespaces.

Out of curiosity, why using 1 core works and not with more? Rcpp code not finding them?

Cheers,

Denis
